math-slopes-areas-s1.title: A rising weather balloon
math-slopes-areas-s1.text: A student tracks a small weather balloon just after release and records its height above the ground every 2 s. The line through the data is the best-fit line, height = 0.50 t + 1.2 (height in meters, t in seconds).

items.q: Using the best-fit line, what is the slope of the graph, with its unit?

mistakes.why: Value: 0.62 divides a height on the line by a time without subtracting the starting height. Slope uses changes: (6.2 − 1.2) ÷ (10 − 0).
Value: the fraction is upside down. Slope is rise (vertical change) over run (horizontal change).
Value: 0.53 m/s is the slope between the first and last data points. Those two points carry their own scatter; use two points on the best-fit line, (0 s, 1.2 m) and (10 s, 6.2 m).

why.correct: Pick two points on the best-fit line, far apart, not data points: (0 s, 1.2 m) and (10 s, 6.2 m). Slope = rise/run = (6.2 m − 1.2 m) ÷ (10 s − 0 s) = 0.50 m/s.

items.q: What does the slope of this graph tell you about the balloon?
options: The rate its height increases (m/s)
How high it is at each moment of its flight
How many seconds it takes to reach 6.2 m
How high above the ground it started

why.correct: A slope means "change in y per change in x". Here that is meters of height per second: the rate at which the balloon rises.
options: Right: the slope is a change in height per change in time, so it is the balloon's upward speed.
Height at a moment is read straight off the graph, not from the slope.
That is a time read from the horizontal axis, not a rate.
The starting height is the vertical intercept, 1.2 m.

items.q: What does the vertical intercept of the best-fit line, 1.2 m, represent?
options: How fast the balloon rises
The total height the balloon gained in 10 s
The error in the height measurements made
Its height when timing began

why.correct: For a line y = mx + b, b is the value of y at x = 0. Timing started with the balloon already 1.2 m up.
options: That is the slope, 0.50 m/s.
The gain is 6.2 m − 1.2 m = 5.0 m, a change, not the intercept.
The intercept is a real starting value: the balloon was released from a height above the ground.
Right: the intercept is the value of y when x is zero.

items.q: Why is the slope found from the best-fit line instead of from the first and last data points?
options: The data points are not plotted on the graph
Two data points are not enough to give a slope
The line averages the scatter of all six points
The best-fit line passes through each of the data points

why.correct: Real data scatter. The first and last points here give (6.4 − 1.1) ÷ 10 = 0.53 m/s, while the best-fit line, which balances points above and below it, gives 0.50 m/s from all six measurements.
options: They are plotted; the issue is that each one carries some random error.
Any two points give a slope, but two scattered points give a less reliable one than a line fit to all six.
Right: each point has some measurement error; the best-fit line uses all the data, so its slope is more reliable.
A best-fit line usually passes between points, with about as many above as below.

items.q: If the balloon keeps rising the same way, what height does the best-fit line predict at t = 14 s?

mistakes.why: Value: 7.0 m is only the height gained after release. Add the starting height, 1.2 m.

items.q: A graph of speed against time is a horizontal line at 2.5 m/s from t = 0 to t = 14 s. What is the area under the line, which is the distance covered?

mistakes.why: Value: an area multiplies the height by the width; you divided.
Value: an area multiplies the two sides; dividing gives a time per speed, not a distance.

why.correct: Area of the rectangle = height × width = 2.5 m/s × 14 s = 35 m. Units: (m/s)(s) = m.

items.q: A graph has speed (m/s) on the vertical axis and time (s) on the horizontal axis. Which unit does the slope have, and which unit does the area under the line have?
options: Slope: m; area: m/s²
Slope: m/s; area: m/s
Slope: s/m; area: m·s²
Slope: m/s²; area: m

why.correct: Slope units = (y unit)/(x unit); area units = (y unit) × (x unit).
options: These are swapped: a slope divides the units, an area multiplies them.
The axis unit alone is neither; slope and area combine both axes' units.
Slope is y over x, not x over y, and an area multiplies y by x.
Right: slope = (m/s) ÷ s = m/s²; area = (m/s) × s = m.

items.q: A graph of speed against time is a straight line from 0 m/s at t = 0 to 8.0 m/s at t = 4.0 s. What is the area under the line from 0 to 4.0 s?

mistakes.why: Value: 32 m is the area of the whole rectangle. The region under a line from zero is a triangle: take half.

why.correct: The region is a triangle: area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 4.0 s × 8.0 m/s = 16 m.

items.q: A cart starts from rest with a steady acceleration, so d = ½at². A student wants a straight-line graph whose slope gives a. What should she plot?
options: d against t; the slope is the acceleration a
d against t²; the slope is ½a
d against t²; the slope is twice the acceleration, 2a
d² against t; the slope is half the acceleration

why.correct: Linearize by matching y = mx: y = d, x = t², m = ½a. Then a = 2 × slope.
options: d against t curves upward because d depends on t², so it has no single slope.
Right: d = (½a)(t²) has the form y = mx with x = t², so the graph is a line through the origin with slope ½a.
The slope is the factor multiplying t², which is ½a, so a = 2 × slope, not slope = 2a.
Squaring d does not undo the square on t; this graph is not a line either.

items.q: A student plots d against t² for a cart released from rest and finds a best-fit slope of 0.36 m/s². Since d = ½at², what is the cart's acceleration?

mistakes.why: Value: the slope is ½a, not a. Multiply the slope by 2.
Value: you halved the slope. The slope already equals ½a, so a = 2 × slope.

why.correct: The slope of d against t² is ½a. So a = 2 × slope = 2 × 0.36 m/s² = 0.72 m/s².
